title: SRE midday digest — EU shift (notes, mitigations, follow-ups)
body:
Shift: EU midday (10:00–14:30 CET)
Owner: Aisha Patel (covering until Jonas takes over at 14:30)
Summary: brief, pragmatic notes for handoff. Focus was a short-lived spike in 503s tied to the KV cache eviction storm affecting the hosted API (/v1/generate) for several customers — impacted latency and triggered auto-fallbacks to smaller model variants for some routes. Incident resolved by manual scale + temporary cache size bump; root cause appears correlated with an anomaly in the cache eviction metric after a deployment that changed tokenization memory usage.

Incidents and timeline:
- 10:12 CET: Alert fired — service: hosted-api-prod, symptom: 5xx-rate > 2% (5m window). PagerDuty pd-89234 triggered.
- 10:14 CET: First triage: traffic distributed across eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; error percent concentrated on requests hitting model variant a-redwood-7b-qa.
- 10:17 CET: Mitigation attempt #1 — route fallback enabled (policy: prefer a-redwood-3b if a-redwood-7b hitting >1.5% 5xx). Observed partial reduction in user-facing errors but tail latency remained elevated.
- 10:22 CET: Investigated KV cache metrics: kv_cache_eviction_rate spiked from ~3/min to ~120/min, kv_cache_miss_rate increased. Suspected eviction storm (likely memory pressure).
- 10:27 CET: Manual scale: increased dedicated serving group for a-redwood-7b by 2 instances (kubectl scale deployment serving-7b-eu --replicas=6). Instances came up by 10:35 CET; error rate returned to baseline by 10:40.
- 11:05 CET: Applied temporary cache-size override (+25%) for the 7b model group to reduce eviction pressure (runbook step: infra cache override). Monitoring shows eviction rate back to normal.
- 11:40 CET: PD incident moved to resolved (root cause investigation continued).

What we observed (metrics):
- Peak 5xx rate: 3.9% at 10:15 CET on /v1/generate for some customers.
- KV cache eviction rate correlates tightly with elevated latency windows.
- Autoscaler did not act quickly enough because scale thresholds are based on CPU rather than kv-cache eviction_OOM signals.

Actions taken (immediate):
- Enabled model fallback routing to smaller variant (mitigation).
- Scaled serving group up in eu cluster (manual).
- Temporary cache-size override applied to reduce evictions.
- Notified on-call dev for model team (Priya Rao) and infra (Jonas Schmidt).
- Created Jira incident: INC-3421 to track RCA and durable fixes.

Open follow-ups (owners + rough ETA):
- SRE: Update autoscaler to include kv_cache_eviction_rate as a scaling metric or add secondary policy (owner: Jonas Schmidt, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- Model infra: Run memory profile for tokenization change in latest model ingest PR (owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 2026-03-16).
- Runbook: Add a concise play for "KV eviction storm" including exact commands used here, thresholds, and rollback steps (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-17).
- Monitoring: Add dashboard panel for kv_cache_miss_rate and set a low-severity alert at 10x baseline (owner: Liam O'Connor, ETA: 2026-03-15).
- QA: Reproduce load pattern in staging with tokenization config from model-PR-212 to confirm memory behavior (owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 2026-03-18).

Runbook notes & commands used (copyable):
- Check 5xx rate (prod): curl -s "https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_server_requests_total{code=~\"5..\"}[5m])" | jq .
- Inspect kv cache (prod): kubectl -n serving exec svc/cache-metrics -- curl http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep kv_cache_eviction_rate
- Manual scale (temporary): kubectl -n serving scale deployment serving-7b-eu --replicas=6 && kubectl -n serving rollout status deployment/serving-7b-eu
- Apply cache override (temporary): infra-cli cache override --model a-redwood-7b --region eu --size-percent +25 --reason "temporary mitigation for eviction storm"
- Revert fallback (when stable): infra-cli routing set-fallback --route /v1/generate --disable --reason "post-incident"

Runbook gaps discovered:
- No explicit section for kv cache eviction storms — current runbooks assume CPU/memory autoscaling only.
- No standardized post-incident traffic replay steps to validate fix in staging that match prod tokenization config.
- Alert thresholds for kv_cache_miss_rate are absent (we only have cache hit ratio panels).

Customer impact notes:
- Affected customers: several small-to-medium hosted API customers routed through a-redwood-7b; no enterprise SLA customers reported escalations during the window. Support ticket queue shows 7 tickets logged between 10:20–11:00 CET; CS triage assigned ticket batch to Tier 1.

Communication and Escalations:
- Slack: #sre-ops posted incident summary at 10:25 CET and updates at 10:40, 11:10.
- Email: Short incident note to infra-owners sent at 11:15 CET.
- No exec-level escalation required.

Post-incident recommendations (prioritized):
1) Short term: Add kv_cache_eviction_rate alert (severity: low) and add autoscaler policy to scale on eviction pressure.
2) Medium term: Expand the autoscaler metrics to include memory pressure signals from model runtime, and add a canary rollout that tracks eviction/miss rate per-deploy.
3) Long term: Consider introducing a per-tenant KV cache quota and smarter eviction policy for heavy tokenization workloads.

Notes for next shift (handoff):
- Jonas taking over at 14:30 CET — key items to check on start: alerts for kv_cache_eviction_rate, status of infra PR #784 (cache autoscaler prototype), and any new model PRs that touched tokenization configuration.
- If 5xx > 1% after 5m: immediately enable fallback for affected route + open a PagerDuty incident.
- If eviction_rate > 50/min sustained 3m: apply temporary cache override (see command above) and escalate to infra team.

Attachments / evidence (copied links):
- Grafana panel (kv cache + 5xx): https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/kv-eviction-playback
- Incident Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3421
- Infra PR (prototype autoscaler change): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/784

Handoff checklist (quick):
- [x] Incident acknowledged and PD resolved
- [x] Temporary mitigations applied (scale + cache override)
- [x] Owners notified (model + infra)
- [ ] Runbook created (draft in progress)
- [ ] Autoscaler change merged (PR open, needs review)

Anything else for evening shift: please watch for regression after autoscaler PR merges; we should not revert the cache override until the autoscaler can handle eviction pressure.

End of notes — Aisha (covering until 14:30 CET).
